source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Configure DDR5 PMIC error handling, enumerate valid UMC targets, inject a rail-type-1 fatal PMIC error, observe the immediate reset, and repeat independently for every DIMM with voltage types 0 and 1.
procedure_facts: Apply ten source-listed PFH, PMIC and I2C BIOS settings and unlock the CPU through HDT.
Boot Ubuntu 20.04, RHEL 9.0 or Windows Server 2022 and retain `--listvalidumc` output.
The example command targets socket:die:UMC 0:0:3, rail type 1, voltage type 0 and DIMM 0.
The system is expected to reset immediately after each fatal injection.
Repeat the setup/injection flow for all DIMMs and both voltage types 0 and 1.
criteria_facts: The tool reports PASS for each uncorrectable error.
The selected OS reports the error within a defined timeout.
The AMD RAS specification governs event and injection-report interpretation.
source_conflicts: Windows Server 2022 is allowed, but the procedure and criteria universally require Linux `dmesg` evidence.
The title calls the fault SWB and fatal while the criteria say only uncorrectable; the source does not define the tool-build mapping from `railtype 1` to SWB or the meanings of `voltagetype 0/1`.
missing_source_information: Tool-build semantics for rail type 1, voltage types 0 and 1, and the expected fatal record.
Selected OS-native evidence query, timeout and correlation fields.
Per-run PMIC health, recovery and restoration criteria.

original_test_intent.statement: Validate the platform's fatal DDR5 PMIC SWB handling for every approved DIMM and both source voltage types by executing one mapped injection at a time, observing the required reset and proving a fresh native-OS fatal record plus recovered PMIC, memory and system health.
must_preserve: Every in-scope DIMM multiplied by voltage types 0 and 1.
Rail type 1 only after the owner confirms it denotes SWB for the exact tool and platform.
One fatal injection and immediate-reset observation per matrix row.
Independent tool PASS and timely OS-native error evidence per run.
360/120 minutes as planning estimates, not evidence timeouts.
must_not_infer: That the example tuple 0:0:3/DIMM 0 addresses every physical DIMM.
That voltage types 0 and 1 have known electrical meanings without the signed recipe.
That Linux dmesg is valid Windows evidence.
That a reset or tool PASS alone proves the requested PMIC fault was handled correctly.
That all matrix rows may be auto-looped after a fatal reset.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly treats the case as a gated hybrid, preserves every-DIMM/two-voltage coverage, requires target mapping, prohibits batching and assigns PMIC/HDT/recovery work to qualified staff.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 mixes Linux-only dmesg/BERT/rasdaemon expectations into the allowed Windows branch, accepts SWB/rail/voltage semantics without tool-version proof, and does not turn the example tuple into a signed per-physical-DIMM matrix with a fresh post-reset evidence boundary.

related_records: Other AMD memory, fabric and PMIC variants cannot establish this row's private SWB rail/voltage semantics or DIMM matrix.
applicable_history.precedence_application: The exact source row controls all-DIMM/two-voltage coverage and the reset expectation; the missing private-tool meanings remain owner-supplied facts rather than public-document assumptions.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Retain the gated hybrid classification. Resolve SWB/rail/voltage semantics and one native OS evidence branch, build a signed every-DIMM-by-two-voltage target matrix, and execute each fatal reset case only after independent approval and recovery gating.

conditions_present: The source supplies the BIOS profile, tool family, command form, reset expectation and every-DIMM-by-two-voltage coverage.
missing: Signed SWB/rail/voltage definitions, complete target matrix, exact tool/hash, selected OS branch, expected native event fields, timeout, approval, recovery and final health gates.
provider: AMD/ODM FAE supplies private tool semantics, PMIC recipe, expected fatal signature and recovery.
Memory/platform owner supplies the populated-DIMM inventory and physical-to-logical target matrix.
Test owner selects the supported OS evidence branch and timeout; lab owner provides the dedicated SUT and per-run approvals.
safe_read_only_work: Inventory platform, firmware, PMIC-capable ECC RDIMMs, serials and physical slots.
Capture current BIOS values, PMIC/thermal/power/memory health and native OS/BMC baselines without clearing logs.
Run the signed non-mutating `--listvalidumc` enumeration and reconcile it to the physical population.
prohibited_until_resolved: BIOS or PMIC/I2C changes, HDT unlock, log clear, fault injection, reset/power recovery, automatic retry, next-matrix-row continuation or restoration.
closure_evidence: Signed tool documentation binds rail type 1 to SWB and defines both voltage types for this platform.
Every physical DIMM has a unique approved tuple for each of the two voltage types.
One OS-native event rule, timeout, per-run approval, recovery and restoration checklist are accepted.

revision_candidate.test_name: AMD DDR5 PMIC SWB Fatal Injection Across All DIMMs and Both Voltage Types
revision_candidate.purpose: For every approved physical DDR5 ECC DIMM and each source voltage type 0 and 1, inject one owner-defined rail-type-1 SWB fatal PMIC error and verify the expected reset, independent tool PASS, fresh native-OS fatal evidence and recovered PMIC, memory and system health.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the AMD platform/stepping, BIOS/BMC/firmware, PMIC-capable DDR5 ECC RDIMM population, selected Ubuntu 20.04, RHEL 9.0 or Windows Server 2022 branch, HDT method and AMD RAS Error Injection Tool build covered by the signed recipe.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The Cartesian set of every owner-approved populated physical DIMM and `voltagetype` 0 and 1. Each row must bind physical slot/serial to socket, die, UMC and tool DIMM index; `0:0:3`, DIMM 0 and voltage type 0 are only the source example. Use `railtype 1` only after signed confirmation that it means SWB. Treat 360/120 minutes as estimates.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Exact tool build/hash and signed definitions of SWB, rail type 1 and voltage types 0/1; complete physical-slot/serial/socket/die/UMC/dimm matrix; ten BIOS values and restore plan; HDT procedure; selected OS-native fatal-event query and expected identity/severity fields; a signed decision whether BMC evidence is mandatory, platform-conditional or supporting-only, plus its required fields when applicable; timeout; reset/recovery/PMIC-health rules; per-row approval and evidence storage.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Preserve complete platform, PMIC, memory, OS and BMC baselines before any approved log clear or use a timestamp marker. A qualified operator applies the ten signed BIOS values and HDT unlock. Boot exactly one approved OS, retain full `--listvalidumc` output and reconcile every matrix row. For one approved row only, run `sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --einjpmicerrors --socketdieumc <signed_socket:die:umc> --railtype 1 --voltagetype <0_or_1> --dimm <signed_index>`, observe the source-required immediate reset, then collect fresh tool, reset, native-OS, BMC and health evidence. Restore or revalidate the recipe state after reboot, obtain go/no-go, and only then proceed to the next independently approved row. Restore all modified state after the final row.
revision_candidate.preconditions: SWB/rail/voltage semantics and full matrix resolved; exact platform, tool, OS and BIOS profile approved; dedicated non-production SUT; stable PMIC/power/thermal/memory baseline; console/OOB, boot media, storage and recovery proven; every BIOS, HDT, clear, injection, reset, next-row and restoration action authorized.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Platform/firmware/OS/tool identities and hashes; physical DIMM population and signed tuple matrix; signed rail/voltage definitions; BIOS/HDT before/during/after; baseline/clear audit and full valid-UMC enumeration; for every matrix row, exact command/transcript, tool PASS, reset and boot timeline, fresh target-correlated native-OS fatal PMIC record within timeout, PMIC voltage/power/thermal and DIMM health, anomalies, recovery, go/no-go and restored final state. Include a fresh target-correlated BMC record only when the signed platform recipe makes it mandatory; otherwise record that BMC evidence is conditional or supporting-only and preserve any available observations without treating their absence as failure.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The signed AMD/ODM PMIC SWB fatal-injection recipe and AMD RAS acceptance rule for the exact platform and tool build. Each physical-DIMM/voltage row passes only when the tool reports PASS, the expected immediate reset occurs, a fresh native-OS fatal record identifies the intended target within timeout, and prescribed PMIC/memory/system recovery gates pass. A BMC record is an additional pass gate only when the signed recipe explicitly requires it and defines its fields and timeout.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Critical PMIC fault injection on a dedicated SUT only. Do not guess tuple, rail or voltage semantics; copy the example tuple across DIMMs; mix Linux and Windows evidence; batch, auto-loop or auto-retry fatal cases; target production or boot-critical data without recovery; expose secrets; truncate logs; or continue after wrong target/severity, failed/looping reset, boot failure, PMIC/voltage/thermal anomaly, DIMM loss, error storm or incomplete restoration.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: AMD/ODM FAE approves tool semantics, target matrix, expected fatal event and recovery; platform/memory owner approves every physical target and BIOS profile; qualified staff perform BIOS/HDT and exceptional recovery. Each injection, post-reset next-row decision and final restoration require recorded approval.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Qualified personnel own physical DIMM identity, BIOS/PMIC/I2C configuration, HDT unlock, console supervision and exceptional power/boot recovery. After exact handoff, an authorized Agent may perform enumeration, a single approved injection and read-only evidence correlation; engineering retains final anomaly and PASS/FAIL judgment.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: After every reset, preserve evidence, verify boot plus PMIC/power/thermal/memory health, revalidate all recipe state that may not survive reset and obtain explicit go/no-go before another row. On failure, use only the signed PMIC/platform recovery, quarantine the affected DIMM if required, restore BIOS/HDT/tool state and prove final health before any separately approved rerun.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved SWB/rail/voltage semantics, target matrix, OS branch or BMC-evidence applicability; enumeration/matrix mismatch; package/BIOS/HDT mismatch; missing approval, timeout, baseline, recovery or storage; wrong target/severity; absent tool PASS, reset or timely native record; absent required BMC record when the signed recipe makes it a pass gate; reset loop, boot failure, PMIC/power/thermal anomaly, DIMM loss, persistent fault or error storm; or failed recovery/restoration/final health.

identified_defects: The source offers Windows but requires dmesg universally.
SWB, rail type 1 and voltage types 0/1 are not defined for the exact private tool build.
The example 0:0:3/DIMM-0 tuple is insufficient for the required all-DIMM matrix.
Fatal versus generic uncorrectable event identity and acceptance fields are underspecified.
V2 does not explicitly require a fresh evidence boundary and recipe-state revalidation after every reset.
reason_for_change: Convert an example PMIC command into the source-required per-DIMM/two-voltage fatal-reset matrix without inventing private SWB semantics, mixing OS evidence or allowing one reset to stand in for target-correlated proof.

new_technical_evidence.title: Querying the System Event Log for Hardware Error Events
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Windows Server 2022 branch allowed by the source
new_technical_evidence.supports: Windows hardware error evidence is queried from Windows Event Log providers; Linux dmesg is not a Windows-native evidence path.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The exact Windows PMIC/WHEA provider and record fields remain platform-specific.

new_technical_evidence.title: Revision Guide for AMD Family 19h Models 90h-9Fh Processors
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Only when the tested CPU family/model and affected condition match
new_technical_evidence.supports: Some documented fatal-error conditions may impair reset/shutdown and require BMC recovery, supporting an explicit family-specific recovery gate rather than assuming reboot success.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The source row does not identify a processor model or show that the documented condition applies.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-System RAS-00809-V002
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Only this DDR5 PMIC SWB fatal row
new_technical_evidence.supports: The BIOS settings, sample command, immediate reset and all-DIMM/two-voltage repetition requirement.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Private rail/voltage semantics, full target matrix, native event signatures, timeout and recovery are absent.

removed_ambiguities: Defines the source coverage as every physical DIMM multiplied by two voltage types.
Marks the literal tuple as an example rather than a reusable target.
Requires a single selected native OS evidence branch.
Makes BMC evidence a signed platform-specific decision rather than an unexplained universal pass gate.
Separates reset observation, tool PASS, target-correlated fatal record and health recovery as independent gates.
resolved_blockers: Tool, matrix, semantics, OS evidence and approval are provider-closable; the case remains REQUIRES rather than technically BLOCKED.
remaining_blockers: Execution awaits signed private-tool semantics, a complete target matrix, one native evidence rule, timeout, authorization and recovery plan.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves V2's correct hybrid controls while proving the exact all-DIMM-by-two-voltage scope, eliminating cross-OS evidence, preventing example-tuple reuse and requiring a fresh post-reset evidence and health gate for every run.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The first contract-only pass recovered the full 2N matrix, target mapping and per-reset gates but found BMC evidence applicability undefined. After Required Inputs, Expected Evidence, Acceptance and Stop Conditions made BMC evidence mandatory only when the signed platform recipe defines it, revalidation found no remaining document defect.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Reliability row 89 requires rail-type-1 fatal PMIC injection for all DIMMs and both voltage types 0 and 1, with an immediate reset per run.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 preserves the matrix concept and manual safety boundary but leaves private SWB semantics, Windows-native evidence and post-reset freshness/state revalidation unresolved.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow read-only inventory, valid-UMC enumeration and baseline capture; prohibit BIOS/HDT/injection/reset progression until semantics, matrix, native evidence, approvals and recovery are signed.
